summary: Every console page of the app's lane copy (the mold plus the app's packs), served on this machine by the lane world (molds/mold_v0/testing/console/, as the accessibility lane), at a phone (390px), a tablet (820px) and a desktop (1440px) width, with a row per pack and a row per page and width. `layout.viewports`: a page that scrolls sideways fails (the element that sticks out is named), as does an HTTP error, an error page, a signed-in page that sends its person to sign-in or a page with no control to use. `tap.targets` (phone and tablet): a control under 24x24 CSS px with another control within 12px of its centre fails (WCAG 2.2 2.5.8; the spacing and inline-link exceptions are named in the detail column). Static measurements only: no timing budget, so a busy machine cannot fail a row.

requires.else: Install the browser this lane drives: npm i -g playwright && npx playwright install chromium.

checks.name: layout.viewports

checks.why: A page that scrolls sideways on a phone hides half of every row and every button past the edge: the person cannot finish the task on the device they own.

not_covered: The DEPLOYED console. These pages are the app's lane copy (build/<app_id>.lane/: the mold plus the app's packs, unbranded), built with `next build --webpack` and served by `next start` on 127.0.0.1 against the lane copy's own API on an embedded throwaway database: the same pages, components and styles the app ships, not the bytes Vercel or its server serves. The brand overlay (name, colour, logo) is graded by `branding.py check`, not here, so colour contrast is measured in the shell's own theme.

Clerk itself. A copy served on this machine cannot reach Clerk with the app's keys, so the console is built with a lane stand-in for `@clerk/nextjs` (molds/mold_v0/testing/console/clerk-standin/, in that build only) that reads the session the shell's own offline Clerk signs; the API verifies that session as it does in production. Clerk's sign-in and sign-up widgets (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-up), its user menu and organisation switcher popups are therefore not graded.

One identity and an empty workspace: the owner of one fresh workspace who is also platform staff. Pages are graded with no records, runs, keys or members (their empty states), and what a member, a viewer or a second workspace sees is not graded.
Dynamic pages with an identifier in the address (a record, an account, a docs article: /app/records/<area>/<key>, /admin/accounts/<slug>, /app/docs/<slug>) are not graded; their list pages are.
Real devices, networks and fingers: Chromium's mobile emulation sets the width, touch and pixel ratio; it does not reproduce a slow CPU, a software keyboard covering a field, or a browser's own bars.
Interaction latency, layout shift and timing of any kind (this lane measures layout only, so a busy shared machine cannot fail it). Orientation changes, zoom to 200-400% and print layout.
WCAG 2.5.8's 'equivalent control elsewhere', 'user agent control' and 'essential' exceptions, which a harness cannot judge; the exceptions it does apply are named per row.
A pack that adds no console page has no row of its own to grade; its row says `not-covered (adds no console page)`, never pass.
